transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been forgetting little things more than I used to. Like, things I normally handle—returning phone calls, turning in a registration form, or remembering to stop for an errand on the way home. It’s been enough that I thought I should ask for help.
Have you ever had a head injury or trauma, such as a concussion or something more serious, that might be relevant to your memory issues?
Not that I can think of. I don’t remember ever having a concussion or any serious head injury.
Have you noticed any other changes besides your memory, like difficulty with planning, organizing, or completing tasks, or any changes in your mood or behavior?

Yeah, I’ve noticed it more with organizing and figuring out what to do first. I can usually keep up at work, but since I started evening classes too, things pile up—my desk, my class folder, even my email reminders. Then I spend a lot of time just sorting through it all instead of actually getting started.
Have you been feeling more down, sad, or irritable lately, or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy?
I don’t think so, no. I mean, I get frustrated when I fall behind on things, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling sad or losing interest in things I normally like.
Have you had trouble handling everyday tasks like cooking, managing finances, or following a recipe that you used to manage easily before?

Not so much cooking or bills, but everyday things, yeah. What finally made me ask for help was I kept forgetting small stuff I usually handle—like returning calls, turning in a registration form, or remembering to stop for an errand on the way home. It’s little things, but they keep slipping.
Has your memory or difficulty organizing tasks affected your performance at work or in your classes?

Yeah, a little. I’m still getting by, but I’ve missed some small follow-ups at work and a few school deadlines. Not huge things, but enough that I’m worried people will start seeing me as unreliable. I’d really like to move toward an Office Manager role, and I’m afraid this could hurt my chances.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to make decisions, solve problems, or stay focused on a task compared to before?

Yeah, mostly with staying focused. I don’t think my decision-making is that different, but at the office or in class, it doesn’t take much to throw me off. Like if a phone rings, or people are talking near me, or I suddenly think of something I need to do at home, I can lose track of what I was working on.
Have you had trouble starting tasks, coming up with a plan to get things done, or knowing how to break a big task into smaller steps?

Yeah, somewhat. I can start things, but when there’s a lot at once I don’t always know what to tackle first. Since I started evening classes, my desk and my class folder and even my email reminders kind of turn into piles. I’ll sit there wasting time just trying to figure out what I’m supposed to do next.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with memory and staying focused—have they been getting worse over weeks, months, or longer?

It’s been more like longer than just a few weeks. I’d say it became noticeably harder to manage after I started my evening certificate program, about 15 months ago. Since then the focus and organizing stuff has been harder to keep up with.
Do these issues with focus and organization happen in different places—like at work, at home, and during your classes—or are they limited to just one setting, like when you're at work or school?

I’m not totally sure how to separate it out. I notice it most when I’m trying to keep up with work or class stuff, but at home I can get scattered too. It’s just more obvious when there are deadlines or a lot of things to keep track of.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated when you need to focus on a task?
Yeah, a little. During longer classes especially, I’ll catch myself clicking my pen or bouncing my foot. I also shift around in the chair a lot, even when I’m trying to sit still and pay attention.
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble staying focused or organizing tasks even when you were a child, like in grade school?

Yes, I think so. In elementary school I was always the kid forgetting permission slips or losing homework somewhere in my backpack. For bigger projects, I usually needed my mom or the teacher to kind of walk me through it step by step or remind me what to do next.

Besides what you’ve noticed recently, do you find that you still tend to act quickly without thinking things through, or feel the need to constantly be doing something, even when you know you should slow down?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think of myself as acting without thinking a lot. I can get kind of antsy if I’m sitting too long, but I wouldn’t say I feel like I have to constantly be doing something.
Looking back, did you often feel very restless or have trouble staying still during childhood, even when you were not under pressure to focus, like at home or during playtime?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember being especially restless at home or during playtime. I think I could sit and play if I was interested in something. Nothing really stands out to me that way.

In your adult life, before starting your evening classes, did you often find yourself struggling to finish tasks, avoiding things that require sustained mental effort, or losing focus easily—even in situations where there wasn’t a lot of pressure or deadlines?

Yeah, I think so. If something meant sitting down to read a long chapter or write out a plan, I’d put it off and put it off. Then it would get late, and I’d end up rushing through it after work. It wasn’t always because there was a deadline right away—I just had a hard time getting myself to start and stay with it.
Do you often feel an inner sense of restlessness, like your mind is constantly going, even when you're not in a situation that requires focus or activity?

I’m not sure I’d call it restlessness. My mind can wander, but I don’t really notice it as constantly going all the time when I’m just sitting around. It’s more like I get distracted sometimes, but not really that driven feeling.

Do you find that your difficulty staying focused happens even when you're doing things you enjoy, like watching a movie or reading something for fun, or does it mostly happen when you're under pressure or have a lot to do?

It mostly shows up when I’m at the office or in class, when I’m trying to focus on something. Like, if a phone rings, or people are talking nearby, I’ll lose my place. Sometimes even just a random thought about something I need to do at home pulls me away from what I was working on.
Do you also notice these same difficulties with staying focused and organizing tasks at home, even when you're not under pressure from work or school deadlines?

Yeah, I do notice it at home too, especially now with the evening classes. I can usually keep up at work, but my desk and my class folder kind of turn into piles, and then my email reminders stack up. I end up spending time just trying to figure out what I’m supposed to do first instead of actually doing it.
When you were a child, did you have trouble staying focused or organizing tasks in more than just school—like at home or with friends—or was it mostly in school settings?

It wasn’t only school. Even in elementary school, I’d forget permission slips or lose homework somewhere in my backpack. At home, my mom had to remind me step by step to finish projects, and teachers did that too. So it was kind of the same pattern in more than one place.

When you were a child, did you have trouble staying focused or organizing tasks not only in school and at home, but also in other settings, like when you were with friends or participating in activities outside the house?

I’m trying to remember outside of school and home… what stands out most is still that same pattern. In elementary school I was always the kid forgetting permission slips, losing homework in my backpack, and needing my mom or the teacher to walk me through projects step by step.
